Cc: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@aequitas.com>

Subject: Aequitas — model affinity & routing guarantee (renewal dependency)

Hi team,

Quick context: Aequitas (AEQ-4721) is in final renewal negotiation — they 
explicitly asked for a written guarantee that production traffic for their account 
will be routed to a single model variant (and pinned model-weights/quantization) 
for the duration of their contract, with a documented fallback behavior. This is 
to satisfy downstream audit requirements and to avoid any micro-drift in outputs.

Their asks are:
- A model-affinity policy (per-tenant pin) so requests prefer an explicit 
  model variant (e.g., redwood/gpt-j-3b-q4f)
- A documented fallback sequence and SLAs if that variant is unavailable
- Additional request-level telemetry (model_id + kernel-profile) retained for 12 months

They've tied this to the renewal (Q3 close). Procurement sent an SLA worksheet 
(attached) and redlines on master (attached). Emily is looped for any clarifying 
questions.

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate whether we can support a formal "model-affinity 
routing policy" as a prioritized change? If not fully feasible, what is the 
recommended compromise and a realistic time-to-delivery (weeks)?

I can push commercial credit/commitment to buy priority if that helps.

Thanks — Connor
Connor Obrien
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: AEQ_SLA_request.xlsx, contract_redlines_v3.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aequitas — model affinity & routing guarantee (renewal dependency)

Connor — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions from Product: 

1) Scope: do they require the affinity to be enforced at request time (hard pin) or is 
   a soft-preference acceptable (best-effort routing with fallback)?
2) Fallback: what failures are acceptable to them (region failover, model-upgrade, 
   capacity shortage)?
3) Telemetry: confirm retention window (12 months) and whether they need token-level
   payloads or just model_id + timing + kernel/profile meta.

From a product standpoint, we have a couple of potential approaches:
- Policy layer: per-tenant routing tags + priority table (low infra effort, high config)
- Runtime affinity: guarantee routing to pinned instances (higher infra work, stronger guarantee)

Ben / Priyom — can you sketch feasibility and a rough ETA for each approach (config-only 
policy vs runtime affinity) and call out audit/ops concerns?

Emily — tagging you to ensure we capture Aequitas' exact risk/acceptance criteria.

—Laura
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@aequitas.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aequitas — model affinity & routing guarantee (renewal dependency)

On Thu, Jul 27, 2028 at 09:08 AM Laura Bennett wrote:
> Ben / Priyom — can you sketch feasibility and a rough ETA for each approach...

Short answer: feasible both ways, tradeoffs below.

1) Config-only policy (routing tags + preference): 
   - Implementation: add per-tenant routing tag and a preference table in the routing 
     layer. Requests tagged = tenant -> routing prefers pinned model variants if available. 
   - Guarantees: best-effort affinity. If pinned variant capacity is exhausted, routing 
     falls back to compatible variant.
   - Effort: ~2 engineer-weeks (routing + admin UI update) + 1 QA week. Can be delivered 
     as a minor release (canary -> prod).

2) Runtime hard-affinity (instance-level pinning): 
   - Implementation: extend scheduler to reserve warm instances for tenant+model, ensure 
     requests are dispatched only to those instances. Requires KV cache isolation and 
     billing mapping changes.
   - Guarantees: strong claim — we can state "requests routed to pinned model instances 
     except for force-maintenances or region-wide failures".
   - Effort: ~8-10 engineer-weeks + infra provisioning + capacity planning. Needs 
     product design for edge cases and cost modelling.

Telemetry retention: we can add model_id, kernel_profile, and timing in the request logs; 
storing enriched telemetry for 12 months is straightforward but will add to log storage costs.
Estimate: 1 engineer-week + additional storage (we should get numbers from infra).

Recommendation: deliver the config-only policy fast (2-3 weeks) as a documented 
commitment with an optional follow-up program to implement runtime hard-affinity 
(if customer pays for reserved capacity). That buys us time and addresses their audit 
needs in the near term.

I'll volunteer to scope the config-only change and draft the product note that Connor 
can present to Aequitas.

—Ben
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Aequitas — model affinity & routing guarantee (renewal dependency)

Thanks Ben — that roadmap split looks reasonable and aligns with our commercial options.
Two notes from the field:
- Aequitas prefers a documented commitment they can show to internal audit even if the initial 
  mechanism is "config-only". They'd like explicit wording in the MSA addendum about the 
  preference policy and fallback ordering.
- They are willing to sign an initial 12-month reserved capacity add-on (committed spend) 
  that would fund the runtime hard-affinity work, but only if we can commit to a 
  delivery milestone (target: T+10 weeks) and a small credit if delivery slips.

Can Product/Legal draft an addendum template we can present to them this week? I can 
soft-commit the reserved capacity verbally, but we need a formal path.

Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

> Attachment references: AEQ_SLA_request.xlsx (detailed retention + audit asks)

From: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@aequitas.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aequitas — model affinity & routing guarantee (renewal dependency)

Connor / Laura / Ben — appreciate the quick turn. To be explicit on acceptance criteria from 
our audit team: 

1) Near-term (must-have before renewal): a documented per-tenant preference policy that 
   routes to pinned model variants when available, with a clear fallback order and 
   an operations runbook describing how incidents are escalated and communicated.
2) Mid-term (target T+10 weeks): hard-affinity option available for purchase (reserved 
   capacity) with a delivery milestone and small SLA credit if missed.
3) Telemetry: model_id + kernel_profile + request latency logged and retained for 12 months.

If Redwood can give us a product note and a draft MSA addendum describing 1) and a plan 
for 2) by end-of-week, procurement will expedite. I'm attaching the SLA worksheet with 
preferred language highlighted.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Shaw
Director of Platform Risk, Aequitas Financial

Attachments: AEQ_SLA_request.xlsx (highlighted)
